attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The Yang-Mills analysis has not proved the required boundary OPE with A=0, nonzero controllable B, and either direct q>=0 or a continuous Hadamard semigroup for Wilson collar quotients. Non-Abelian path ordering and connected fields spanning adjacent collar layers may break the semigroup.
steps: Fix a finite locked Wilson family and move each observable to a positive collar. Regulated reflection positivity gives N^\delta\ge0.
Use the RG topology to pass to N=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}N^\delta, so N\ge0 by closedness of the positive matrix cone.
Write the boundary OPE as N=B\circ M+A. Diagonal trace continuity gives A_{ii}=0; if A is a positive additive contact, Cauchy-Schwarz gives A=0.
Normalize diagonals. Then same-theory positivity of M is equivalent to q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B being positive semidefinite on every finite realized block.
For triples, this gives the explicit determinant test 1+2Re(q12 q23 conjugate(q13))-|q12|^2-|q23|^2-|q13|^2>=0, which detects phase and modulus defects missed by pairwise damping.

If collar refinements produce q_{s+t}=q_s\circ q_t, scalar continuity gives q_tij=exp(t ell_ij). Positivity of q_t and the zero-sum condition on c imply 0<=sum cbar_i c_j q_tij=t sum cbar_i c_j ell_ij+o(t), hence ell is CPD.
Conversely, Hermitian CPD ell gives exp(t ell)>=0 by Schoenberg, so the quotient obstruction is removed on that block.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is a valid finite-matrix bridge, not an existence proof. It still needs cutoff-uniform Wilson boundary estimates, OS-density of the locked core, and verification that no boundary counterterm or new boundary Hilbert sector is being smuggled in.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: Wilson boundary Schur-preimage test

assumptions: Fixed-collar reflection positivity and RG convergence give N^\delta\to N with N\ge0 for every finite locked Wilson family.
Diagonal trace continuity holds and any positive additive boundary contact has zero diagonal, hence vanishes on the block.
On the nonzero support graph of B, the collar OPE factorizes as \widehat N=\widehat B\circ\widehat M with B_{ii}=N_{ii}=M_{ii}=1 after normalization.
Optional semigroup certificate: realized collar refinements provide q_t with q_0=1, q_{s+t}=q_s\circ q_t, q_t=q_t^*, and q_t continuous for 0\le s,t,s+t\le1.
definitions: source object: finite families F_i^\delta of gauge-invariant Wilson/hairpin observables in t>\delta, their regulated reflected OS matrices N^\delta_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta), and the multiplicative boundary Gram anomaly B from collar collapse.
target object: the continuum OS matrix M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j) for the same locked Wilson observables at the reflection plane, hence the physical OS pre-Hilbert form after null-vector quotient.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions through finite reflected Wilson quadratic forms, collar trace limits, and q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B.

same-theory condition: observable labels, diagonal Wilson renormalizations, loop/smearing classes, and reflection action are fixed before and after collar removal; dividing by B is valid only when B is an internal trace factor, not a new boundary field or counterterm.

equations.label: collar limit positivity
equations.valid_when: The RG cutoff-removal topology is valid for every reflected finite Wilson probe at fixed positive collar.

equations.label: same-theory Schur preimage
equations.valid_when: B_{ij}\ne0 on the tested block, target diagonals are positive, and additive contacts have been eliminated without changing the theory.

equations.label: three-hairpin determinant falsifier
equations.valid_when: q is a normalized Hermitian 3 by 3 quotient matrix; violation is a finite OS falsifier.

equations.label: log-CPD semigroup certificate
equations.valid_when: A continuous Hadamard collar semigroup exists with a Hermitian logarithm \ell; by Schoenberg this is valid and sufficient for q_t\ge0 for all t\ge0.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Compute a locked Wilson triple with \det(\widehat N\oslash\widehat B)<0, or under a valid semigroup find a zero-sum c with \sum\bar c_i c_j\ell_{ij}<0.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma separates the exact finite obstruction q\ge0 from the stronger infinite-divisibility/log-CPD certificate. It avoids overclaiming that every nontrivial B is fatal.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a locked finite Wilson OS block with additive boundary contacts removed, same-theory OS positivity at the reflection plane is exactly positivity of the normalized Schur quotient q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B. If the quotient is realized by a continuous Hadamard collar semigroup, then this finite test is certified by a Hermitian conditionally positive logarithm.

assumptions: B is Hermitian positive semidefinite with B_{ii}=1 after diagonal normalization.
The multiplicative anomaly model is asserted without adding an independent boundary sector.
The intended OS matrix has finite distributional pairings on the locked test algebra.
definitions: Boundary zero edge: a pair of Wilson boundary footprints for which the normalized multiplicative anomaly B_{ij} vanishes.
Nonzero support graph: the graph with vertices i and edges ij where B_{ij}\ne0.
Compatible Schur preimage: a matrix M with finite entries and N=B\circ M on all tested entries.

equations.label: zero-edge compatibility
equations.valid_when: M_{ij} is finite and the same-theory multiplicative factorization is valid.

equations.label: support-graph reduction
equations.valid_when: Each V_\alpha is a connected component of the nonzero support graph of B; cross-component entries require direct trace control.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A concrete pair with B_{ij}=0 and N_{ij}\ne0 is a falsifier of the multiplicative same-theory bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents a singular boundary anomaly from being hidden inside a formal Schur quotient.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Zeros of the boundary Gram anomaly cannot be ignored: if B_{ij}=0 but N_{ij}\ne0, no finite same-theory target matrix M can satisfy N=B\circ M on that pair.

assumptions: The core is dense in the chosen gauge-invariant OS test algebra without changing observable labels.
For every finite core block, additive contacts vanish and q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B is positive semidefinite, or is certified by log-CPD semigroup data.
The trace modulus is uniform enough to pass positivity from collars to plane-supported limits.
definitions: Mirror-smooth core: gauge-invariant local composites and Wilson observables whose collars approach the reflection plane through reflection-compatible smooth families.
Trace modulus: a bound controlling Q_S(F,c)-Q_S(T_\delta F,c) uniformly for finite OS vectors.
OS-density: convergence in the topology generated by finite reflected quadratic forms.

equations.label: trace modulus
equations.valid_when: The cutoff-removal topology controls reflected probes as their supports enter the reflection-plane collar.

equations.label: closed cone extension
equations.latex: F^{(n)}\to F\text{ in }\tau_{OS},\quad Q(F^{(n)},c)\ge0\ \forall n\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Q(F,c)\ge0
equations.valid_when: \tau_{OS} is the initial topology of the finite reflected quadratic forms.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The core is not OS-dense, or approximating a cusp Wilson loop requires a new boundary renormalization not present in the locked algebra.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Connects the finite Wilson boundary calculation back to the original closed-cone OS passage.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A dense-core promotion theorem is available once the Wilson quotient test is proved on a mirror-smooth gauge-invariant core with a uniform trace modulus.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the same locked gauge-invariant algebra cannot define N, B, and q through collar collapse, or if reflected Wilson products require boundary counterterms.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if additive contacts vanish and every finite dense-core Wilson block satisfies q>=0, preferably via a valid collar semigroup with CPD logarithm plus a uniform trace modulus.
control_decision.reason: The branch made a substantive refinement: it replaced vague boundary anomaly language by an exact Schur-preimage criterion and a conditional semigroup/log-CPD certificate.

dependency_updates.description: The closed-cone step is formal for fixed collars; the remaining bridge is finite Schur-preimage positivity q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B and trace-modulus extension.
The Wilson core must be locked under collar shifts, products, reflection, and the boundary OPE labels; otherwise positivity may be proved for a different theory.
It must control N, diagonal trace continuity, additive contacts, and finite quotient determinants, not only ordinary Schwinger distribution convergence.
Compute B and N for reflected Wilson hairpin blocks; prove q>=0 directly or prove a valid Hadamard semigroup with CPD logarithm.

falsifiers: falsifier: a three-hairpin Wilson block with det(\widehat N\oslash\widehat B)<0, even though all two-by-two minors are nonnegative.
falsifier: under a valid collar semigroup, a zero-sum vector c with \sum\overline c_i c_j\ell_{ij}<0 for the logarithmic quotient kernel.
falsifier: B_{ij}=0 while N_{ij}\ne0, making the Schur preimage singular rather than merely indefinite.
falsifier: the collar quotient fails q_{s+t}=q_s\circ q_t because connected Yang-Mills boundary fields couple the two subcollars.
falsifier: additive contact removal requires a boundary counterterm or Wilson renormalization not present in the locked same-theory algebra.
falsifier: the RG compactness topology is not valid for reflected Wilson products as collars collapse to the reflection plane.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 209 corrects the role of log-CPD. The exact same-theory obstruction is finite positivity of q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B; log-CPD is not automatically necessary for one realized block. It becomes necessary and sufficient only when Wilson collar quotients form a continuous Hadamard semigroup, i.e. an infinite-divisibility structure. The next real work is therefore a boundary OPE calculation that either proves q>=0 on the locked Wilson core or produces a determinant/log-quadratic falsifier.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the leading boundary OPE for three mirror-smooth rectangular Wilson hairpins sharing a reflection-plane footprint. Extract \widehat N, \widehat B, q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B, evaluate the 3 by 3 determinant, and test whether splitting the collar gives q_{s+t}=q_s\circ q_t.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
